::: {#exm-dfs-tree}
#### A depth-first search tree of the town graph

With the adjacency list of @exm-bfs-tree, `dfs` (@def-dfs) from $a$ makes these calls,
each indented under the call that made it:

```text
dfs(W, a)             marks a; its list is b, f, g
  dfs(W, b)           marks b; its list is a, c
    dfs(W, c)         marks c; its list is b, d, g
      dfs(W, d)       marks d; its list is c, e
        dfs(W, e)     marks e; its list is d, f, g
          dfs(W, f)   marks f; a and e are marked, so it returns
          dfs(W, g)   marks g; a, c and e are marked, so it returns
```

After that every vertex is marked, and each call returns in turn.
The depth-first search tree (@def-dfs-tree) from $a$ has the six edges

$$
\set{a, b}, \set{b, c}, \set{c, d}, \set{d, e}, \set{e, f}, \set{e, g},
$$

drawn thick in @fig-hub-dfs.
With root $a$, it has height 5, with $f$ and $g$ at level 5,
while the breadth-first search tree of @exm-bfs-tree has height 3.
The level of $g$ is 5, but $\operatorname{dist}(a, g) = 1$:
unlike the breadth-first search tree, the depth-first search tree does not give distances.

::: {#fig-hub-dfs}
